content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Tempe

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's requirements—which vary based on your degree level—to confirm you meet both components. Gather proof of your education and project hours; you'll need these for your PMI application.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual PMP Bootcamp, delivered by active certified practitioners. Attend all instructor-led sessions on your schedule—no commute required. This formal education satisfies PMI's mandatory contact-hour requirement and builds the framework you'll need to pass the exam.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing bootcamp coursework, submit your PMP application directly to PMI, including your education transcripts and project-experience documentation. Pay the PMI examination fee. PMI will review and approve your eligibility, typically within days. Keep your confirmation handy for exam registration.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's post-bootcamp exam-preparation resources—practice exams, study guides, and instructor support—to reinforce your knowledge. Schedule your exam through Pearson VUE once approved. Sit for the computer-based PMP exam at an authorized testing center or through proctored remote delivery.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: Your PMP is valid for three years. During each three-year cycle, earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, or speaking engagements. Renew your credential with PMI before expiration by submitting your PDU record and renewal fee.
